title: Conjecture 2.4
statement_text: There exists an absolute positive constant $C$ such that for all vectors $a_1,\ldots,a_n,b_1,\ldots,b_n\in\mathbb{R}^n$, each of Euclidean norm at most $1$, and for every $0<\varepsilon<1$ and $t=\lfloor C\log(2+\varepsilon^2 n)/\varepsilon^2\rfloor$, there are vectors $x_1,\ldots,x_n,y_1,\ldots,y_n\in\mathbb{R}^t$ such that $|\langle x_i,y_j\rangle-\langle a_i,b_j\rangle|\le\varepsilon$ for all $i,j$, together with the further requirement that $\|x_i\| \leq O(1)$ and $\|y_i\| \leq O(1)$ for all $1 \leq i \leq n$.
context_text: This is a problem of high-dimensional geometry (dimension reduction and compression of inner products). The authors prove the statement without the norm requirement (a bipartite Johnson–Lindenstrauss-type reduction, with a randomized polynomial-time algorithm), motivated by the suggestion of Larsen and Nelson that for small $\varepsilon$ the Johnson–Lindenstrauss dimension $\frac{\log n}{\varepsilon^2}$ might be improvable to $\frac{\log(2+\varepsilon^2n)}{\varepsilon^2}$. The conjecture asks that the output vectors can moreover be taken of bounded norm. It is trivial for $\varepsilon<\sqrt{C/(2n)}$ (then $t\ge n$), and for $\varepsilon>1/n^{0.49}$ it follows from the Johnson–Lindenstrauss lemma. If true, together with the paper's methods it would determine up to a constant factor $f(n,n,\varepsilon)$, the minimum number of bits needed to store all inner products between $n$ vectors of norm at most $1$ in $\mathbb{R}^n$ up to additive error $\varepsilon$, for all $\varepsilon\ge2/\sqrt n$: the authors currently have $\Omega(nt)\le f(n,k,\varepsilon)\le O(n\log n/\varepsilon^2)$ for $t\le k\le n$, where $t=\log(2+\varepsilon^2n)/\varepsilon^2$. The authors support the conjecture by proving it when $t=\Omega(n)$, i.e. $\varepsilon=\Theta(1/\sqrt n)$, via a Gaussian random construction.
notes: PDF source — norm notation $\|\cdot\|$ appears as bare vertical bars in the raw extract; reconstructed from context. The paper proves two partial results supporting the conjecture: the case $t = \Omega(n)$ (i.e., $\varepsilon = \Theta(1/\sqrt{n})$) is established as Theorem 2.5, and a matching bit-count estimate is proved for the column-query variant.
paper_title: Optimal compression of approximate inner products and dimension reduction

title: Larsen–Nelson Question on Improved Johnson-Lindenstrauss Dimension
statement_text: For any $\varepsilon$, can the target dimension in the Johnson-Lindenstrauss Lemma be improved by replacing $\frac{\log n}{\varepsilon^2}$ with $t = \frac{\log(2 + \varepsilon^2 n)}{\varepsilon^2}$?
context_text: Larsen and Nelson [18] asked whether the Johnson-Lindenstrauss dimension bound $\log n / \varepsilon^2$ can be replaced by the smaller quantity $\log(2+\varepsilon^2 n)/\varepsilon^2$ for small $\varepsilon$. This is non-trivial only for $\varepsilon < 1/n^{0.49}$; the present paper's Theorem 1.2 and the lower-bound results in Corollary 2.3 are explicitly motivated by this question.
paper_contribution: Proves a bipartite version (Theorem 1.2): for any $a_1,\ldots,a_n, b_1,\ldots,b_n \in \mathbb{R}^n$ of norm at most 1 and $t = \lfloor C\log(2+\varepsilon^2 n)/\varepsilon^2 \rfloor$, there exist $x_1,\ldots,x_n, y_1,\ldots,y_n \in \mathbb{R}^t$ with $|\langle x_i, y_j\rangle - \langle a_i, b_j\rangle| \leq \varepsilon$ for all $i,j$, computable in randomized polynomial time. Also proves a matching lower bound (Corollary 2.3) showing no embedding into dimension $o(\log(2+\varepsilon^2 n)/\varepsilon^2)$ is possible for any $\varepsilon \geq 2/\sqrt{n}$.
